A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same novelty-evaluation framework and creative tasks despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures and tables, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-generation experiments, temperature and prompting analyses, and human validation of quality scores.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds OLMo-2 and deduplicated Pythia results, expanded prompting analyses, and a new human-validation study.

M1.justification: The harmonic-mean novelty metric, unseen-n-gram originality measure, novel-ICL selection, Asking prompts, and three-round denial-prompting procedure are retained. The evaluated models and scoring configuration change, but no new generation algorithm or novelty-aggregation rule is introduced.

E1.justification: TinyStories, CoPoet, and MacGyver remain the generation benchmarks. v2 expands the originality-reference corpora to include Dolmino, OLMo-2-Preference, and Tulu RLVR, and adds validation involving writer/teacher annotators and model outputs alongside dataset references (Section 2.3 and Appendix D).

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison set expands substantially with OLMo-2 base/instruct models and Pythia-Deduped models (Tables 1 and 8). Table 4 also introduces comparisons among quality judges, including Claude models, GPT-4.1, o3-mini, and GPT-5-Mini. Original Pythia results are relocated to the appendix, not removed.

E3.justification: The main-text evaluator changes from GPT-4o to five-sample o3-mini scoring, with the stated score range changing from 1–5 to 0–5. Prompting experiments change their stated sample count from 250 to 750 per dataset, and model evaluation extends to 32B. A new validation study uses 100 examples and three annotations per task/example; these reported changes do not establish that unchanged legacy results were recomputed.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-scale comparisons of model families/training variants, extends post-training and prompting analyses across OLMo-2 sizes, and adds Pythia-12B to temperature analysis. Appendix D compares judge models and single-run, ICL, and five-sample scoring configurations. The earlier human-validation study and qualitative case tables remain in later appendices.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies five sampled judge ratings and reports Krippendorff’s alpha and Spearman correlations in its additional validation study. The earlier Pearson analysis and paired t-tests at alpha 0.05 remain. This expands statistical validation and aggregation without establishing additional generation seeds or an increase in earlier run counts.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in Tables 1, 4, 8, and 9. For example, OLMo-2-32B-Instruct has MacGyver quality 0.971 and a reported n=5 novelty difference of +0.198 from the reference baseline; five-sample o3-mini has Spearman correlations of 0.50, 0.52, and 0.52. Legacy numerical results largely persist, although some significance markers disappear, including TinyStories prompting markers in Table 2. New model/setting results should not be interpreted as same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 Section 2.1 corrects v1’s reversed local definition: originality counts n-grams that do not appear in training data, and more unseen n-grams indicate greater distance. This reconciles the definition with the unseen-n-gram metric stated elsewhere in both versions. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract’s broad claim that LLM text is less novel than human text is narrowed to some base LLMs. Improving the underlying model at fixed scale becomes a central finding, while scaling gains are qualified by a plateau at larger sizes. These changes materially revise the paper’s principal empirical claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets fixed-scale model improvements as originality gains, larger-scale results as saturation, and novel-ICL benefits as weak and model-dependent. It adds a substantive proposal for proprietary providers to report aggregate novelty statistics (Appendix C). The earlier restriction to one base/post-trained model pair is removed as the analysis expands.

D1.justification: v2 adds indexing-tool and corpus information, annotator recruitment and screening details, and judge-sampling settings. Its announced generation collection grows from over 2,000 to over 5,000 outputs. However, v1’s explicit code/data repository link is replaced by a promise of availability upon publication; actual external availability cannot be determined from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature supporting OLMo-2, Tulu 3, judge validation, and repeated-sample judging. It removes the Lam et al. concept-induction citation and shortens the comparison with coding-creativity research. The central positioning around memorization, originality, and task-specific quality remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, introduction, results narrative, and conclusion are substantially revised. Metric definition, task descriptions, and operationalization are consolidated into Section 2, with judge validation promoted into the main exposition. Appendices are reorganized, while most prompt text and existing examples remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn into three panels, and the main visual narrative gains separate scaling, post-training, temperature, and prompting plots. Tables are expanded and reorganized, with new illustrative, judge-validation, and multi-size prompting tables. The earlier temperature plot becomes appendix Figure 6, and many qualitative tables are retained with new numbering and formatting.

improvement.justification: The broader model comparisons and systematic judge-validation study strengthen evidence beyond v1’s single post-training pair. However, v2 does not reconcile revised judging/sample protocols with unchanged legacy scores, and new metric columns conflict across tables: OLMo-2-7B TinyStories five-gram originality is 0.758 in Table 1 but 0.580 in Table 2. Replacing the repository link with a future-release statement also weakens reproducibility documentation. These gains and unresolved reporting problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
